text:
maya_support: Hey team, customer (john) opened a ticket about batch /rerank returning candidates that look 'zippered' across multiple queries — e.g. candidate lists are interleaved instead of per-query. customer provided payload + response. can we triage? :eyes:

customer_john: repro steps i used:
1) POST /v1/rerank/batch with body below
2) got 200 but scores don't align with queries
3) small test shows candidate lists are shifted by one for query 2+

customer_john: payload:
```json
{
  "queries": [
    {"id": "q1", "text": "weather today"},
    {"id": "q2", "text": "best hiking trails"},
    {"id": "q3", "text": "coffee shops near me"}
  ],
  "candidates": [
    ["c1","c2","c3"],
    ["d1","d2"],
    ["e1","e2","e3","e4"]
  ],
  "top_k": 3
}
```

customer_john: response (redacted):
```json
{
  "results": [
    {"query_id": "q1", "ranked": ["c1","c2","c3"]},
    {"query_id": "q2", "ranked": ["c3","d1","d2"]},
    {"query_id": "q3", "ranked": ["d2","e1","e2"]}
  ]
}
```

maya_support: note how c3 shows up in q2's top list and d2 shows up in q3. customer says this didn't happen yesterday. started around 09:12 UTC. no auth/billing errors in ticket, but they did say they hit a 429 earlier during unrelated calls.

kevin_ml: thanks. can you paste full request_id and approximate timestamps from their headers? also which SDK/version?

customer_john: request-id: req_01G3X7YYA, sdk: js-client v1.7.2, sent 2026-02-18T09:13:02Z. i can share a larger dump if needed.

maya_support: attaching customer's full dump to thread (private).

ashley_engineer: digging in. quick hypothesis: batching/flattening code may be collapsing candidates into one flat queue and then slicing by global offset rather than per-query lengths. that would produce a zipper effect when queries have uneven candidate counts. :thinking:

kevin_ml: can repro locally using their payload + our v1.7.2 inference runner. running a local batch via `./tools/run_rerank --batch-file customer_dump.json`

kevin_ml: repro confirmed on staging with same SDK version. logs show we create a single flattened candidates array of length 9, then use a map of query offsets but an off-by-one calculation leads to overlapping windows. snippet from logs:
```
flattened_candidates_len=9
query_offsets=[0,3,5] // computed from prefix sums
for i in range(len(queries)):
  start = query_offsets[i]
  end = query_offsets[i+1] // oops when i==len-1 this reads next query_offsets out of bounds -> falls back to implicit sum and wraps
```

ashley_engineer: confirmed bug in rerank/batcher v2.1.0. root cause: when candidate lists are passed as nested lists, the batcher flattens then uses an incorrect end index for the last query when padding/truncation logic runs. producing cross-query leakage.

maya_support: severity? impacted customers count?

kevin_ml: current impact estimate: 4 customers reported in last 3 hours, but logs show ~120 batch-rerank calls with uneven candidate sizes in last 6h across prod region eu-west-1. likely low-ish percent but bad for ranking correctness.

ashley_engineer: workaround for customers: send separate per-query calls (slower but correct) or ensure all candidate arrays are equal length (pad with dummy ids) until we patch. also set `prefer_per_query=true` client-side will avoid batch flatten path. document this as temp mitigation.

maya_support: billing folks — customer asked if these misranks will be refunded. any guidance? @billing-bot

billing-bot: for incidents causing incorrect responses, policy is to review per-case. please capture request-ids and affected timestamps. provisional credit may be offered. create billing ticket with tag `rerank-zipper`.

kevin_ml: i've drafted a fix: change batcher to keep candidate offsets array and compute end via start + original_length rather than reading next offset. unit tests added for uneven lengths and single-query edge cases. PR: https://git.redwood.example/p/rerank-batcher/pull/402 (WIP).

ashley_engineer: running CI now on the branch. also adding an integration test that mirrors customer's dump.

kevin_ml: QA on staging passed for my runs. going to run a 2h canary in eu-west-1 with traffic split 5% -> monitor for misalignments and latency regressions.

maya_support: can we also check whether this interacts with KV-cache or prefix caching paths? might explain why customer said it worked yesterday.

kevin_ml: good call — checked earlier commits: cache invalidation change rolled out yesterday morning; that combined with the flattened path could have exposed the bug for some query shapes. documenting timeline.

ashley_engineer: deployment plan: ship hotfix to batcher service, rollout canary 5% for 2h, then 25% for 1h, then full if no regression. PR ready for review. tagging @sre_bot for rollout.

sre_bot: noted. will coordinate canary windows and watchlists. please provide metrics: misalignment-rate (new CloudWatch metric we emit), 95th latency, error-rate. set paging at misalignment > 0.5% for 1m.

maya_support: updated customer with workaround and ETA for patch (canary start in ~40m). they asked for a republish of their data to repro — we declined and offered to run their dump in staging with their permission.

customer_john: appreciate the quick triage. please keep me posted. i can provide more examples if you need them. thanks! :pray:

kevin_ml: will follow up when canary completes. assigned to ashley_engineer to merge on green.

ashley_engineer: merged, canary started at 2026-02-18T10:02:00Z, 5% traffic. initial metric: misalignment-rate dropped from ~0.8% to 0.0 for canary hosts (first 12m). no latency regressions.

maya_support: closing loop with customer — offered credit per billing-bot guidance and asked for permission to run their dump in staging for regression tests.

customer_john: permission granted, sent secure link. thanks again.

maya_support: after full rollout completed, will add postmortem entry and update docs: add `prefer_per_query` option and recommended padding approach.

kevin_ml: postmortem draft will include root cause, timeline, mitigation, customer list, and followups (add integration tests, improve metrics, SDK change to warn when uneven candidate lists seen).

maya_support: tagging followups: 1) docs note 2) SDK change to warn 3) add metric alert 4) create billing ticket. assigning accordingly.

ashley_engineer: thanks everyone. great cross-team response. :thumbsup:
